Prospect
pros'-pekt
n. (a view; the direction a thing looks — in the Authorized Version, the facing of the temple chambers and gates)
Latin prospicere, to look forward, from pro and specere, to look. In Ezekiel's temple vision the word does not mean expectation but orientation: which way a chamber or a gate looks.

Biblical Definition

In Ezekiel's temple the prospect of a room is its assignment. The chambers by the north gate, “whose prospect is toward the south, is for the priests, the keepers of the charge of the house” (Eze 40:45); and the chamber “whose prospect is toward the north is for the priests, the keepers of the charge of the altar: these are the sons of Zadok among the sons of Levi, which come near to the LORD to minister unto him” (Eze 40:46). Which way a man's chamber faced determined what he kept — the house or the altar — and the sons of Zadok, who had been faithful when the rest of the Levites went astray, are the ones who come near. Faithfulness in a former generation is honoured with nearness in this one. The measuring man then brings Ezekiel “forth toward the gate whose prospect is toward the east” (Eze 42:15) and measures it round about. And then the reason for all the measuring: “the glory of the LORD came into the house by the way of the gate whose prospect is toward the east” (Eze 43:4). The glory that Ezekiel had watched depart from the city by the east in chapter eleven returns by the same gate. God comes back the way He left, and He comes into a house that has been measured and assigned down to the facing of its rooms.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines prospect as view of things within the reach of the eye; and also the place and position of the front of a building, the direction it faces.

expand to see more

PROSPECT, n. View of things within the reach of the eye.

1. View of things to come; view delineated by the mind; as the prospect of better times.

2. Place which affords an extended view.

3. Position of the front of a building; as a prospect toward the south or north.

Key Scripture

Eze 43:4 — "And the glory of the LORD came into the house by the way of the gate whose prospect is toward the east."

Eze 40:46 — "And the chamber whose prospect is toward the north is for the priests, the keepers of the charge of the altar: these are the sons of Zadok among the sons of Levi, which come near to the LORD to minister unto him."

Eze 40:45 — "And he said unto me, This chamber, whose prospect is toward the south, is for the priests, the keepers of the charge of the house."

Eze 42:15 — "Now when he had made an end of measuring the inner house, he brought me forth toward the gate whose prospect is toward the east, and measured it round about."

Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The archaic sense — the direction a building faces — is simply unfamiliar to modern readers, who hear only the sense of expectation. No doctrine turns on the term.

The principle to recover is that God is exact about His house, and that the exactness is a mercy. Eight chapters of Ezekiel are given to measurements — gates, chambers, courts, the facing of every room — delivered to exiles who had watched the first temple burn. The vision does not begin with comfort; it begins with a measuring reed, and the comfort is in the measuring. A God who specifies which way a priest's chamber looks is a God who has not abandoned the project. And the vision ends with the glory returning by the east gate, the way it had gone out. What God removes in judgment He is able to bring back, by the same road.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew panim (H6440), face — the face or facing of a chamber; derek (H1870), way; kabod (H3519), glory.

expand to see more

Hebrew panim (H6440) — face, front; in Ezekiel 40-43 the face of a chamber or gate, rendered prospect.

Hebrew derek (H1870) — way, road, direction; the way of the gate whose prospect is toward the east.

Hebrew kabod (H3519) — glory, weight; Ezekiel 43:4, the glory of the LORD returning to the house.

Hebrew Tsadoq (H6659) — Zadok, righteous; the priestly line kept near because it kept the charge.

Hebrew mishmereth (H4931) — a charge, a watch, a duty kept; what each chamber's occupants were responsible for.

Usage

"“By the way of the gate whose prospect is toward the east” — the glory came back."

"“Whose prospect is toward the north is for the priests… of the altar”."

"“He brought me forth toward the gate… and measured it round about”."
